title: Describing Physical Appearance
description: Describe height, build, hair style, eye colour, and distinctive facial features accurately.
objectives: Use 'to be' for height, build, and age (He is tall, she is young)
Use 'have/has' for hair, eyes, and facial features (He has dark hair, she has brown eyes)
Avoid mixing 'is' and 'has' when describing people

vocabularyList.definition: Of great or more than average height.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: My brother is very tall and plays basketball.

vocabularyList.definition: Measuring a small distance from end to end in height.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: She is shorter than her elder sister.
He maintains a slim build through regular running.

vocabularyList.definition: Made of curls or having a wavy or spiral shape.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The little girl has curly brown hair.

vocabularyList.definition: Extending or moving uniformly in one direction only; without a curve.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: She has long, straight black hair.

vocabularyList.definition: With little or no light; of a deep colour.
Light, blond, or pale in colour.
A growth of hair on the chin and lower cheeks of a man's face.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: My grandfather has a neat white beard.

vocabularyList.definition: Having lived or existed for only a short time.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He is a bright young professional.

vocabularyList.definition: Of a person, old or aging politely.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: We should always respect elderly people.

sections.title: The Split Rule: 'To Be' vs. 'Have / Has'
sections.content:
When describing how someone looks, English makes a strict grammatical division:

### 1. Use 'To Be' (am / is / are) for Overall Body & Age
- Height: *He **is** tall / short / medium height*.
- Build: *She **is** slim / athletic*.
- Age: *They **are** young / elderly*.

### 2. Use 'Have / Has' for Features & Parts
- Hair: *She **has** long straight hair*.
- Eyes: *He **has** brown eyes*.
- Facial features: *He **has** a beard / a moustache*.

callouts.title: Hair Order Rule
callouts.text: When describing hair, order is usually: **Length -> Texture -> Colour**: *She has long (length), curly (texture), black (colour) hair*.

callouts.title: Hair is Uncountable
callouts.text: In English, the hair on someone's head is uncountable! Say: 'She has dark **hair**' (NEVER 'She has dark hairs').

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Use 'to be' for height, build, and age (He is tall, she is slim, they are elderly).
Use 'have/has' for features (She has brown eyes, he has a beard).
Hair descriptive order: Length -> Texture -> Colour (long straight black hair).
Never confuse: He is tall (NOT he has tall); He has dark eyes (NOT he is dark eyes).
